content:
Numbers and operations anchor the Class 4 Maths Olympiad — large numbers, place value, rounding, Roman numerals and the four operations appear across every IMO and SOF paper. This guide covers what the chapter tests, the facts your child needs, the common slips, and a free 10-question online test from our verified bank.

What the Class 4 Maths Olympiad Numbers and Operations chapter tests

  • Large numbers — place value, expanded form and number names
  • Comparing, ordering and rounding
  • Roman numerals (I to M)
  • The four operations with word problems

Key facts your child should know

  • Compare numbers by digits first, then the highest place.
  • Round by the digit to the right of the target place — 5 or more rounds up.
  • Roman numerals: smaller before bigger subtracts (XL = 40); after adds (LX = 60).
  • Dividend = Quotient × Divisor + Remainder; the remainder is less than the divisor.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Misreading the place value in a large number.
  • Rounding by the wrong digit.
  • Choosing the wrong operation in a two-step word problem.

questions.q: A newspaper prints the crowd of 2,64,718 rounded to the nearest 1,000. Which number appears?
questions.explanation: 2,64,718 lies between 2,64,000 and 2,65,000; it is nearer to 2,65,000, so it rounds to 2,65,000.

questions.q: 6,003 chocolates are shared equally among 7 friends. How many chocolates remain unshared?
questions.explanation: 6,003 ÷ 7 gives quotient 857 (7 × 857 = 5,999), so the remainder is 4.

questions.q: A factory makes 1,275 toys every day. In 25 days, 348 toys are found defective and removed. How many good toys are left?
13,508 + ▢ = 60,204. Which number goes in the box?
Zoya rounds 8,462 and 5,317 to the nearest 1,000 and then subtracts them. What answer does she get?
847 mangoes are packed equally into 7 crates. How many mangoes go into each crate?
A rope 7,215 metres long is cut into 5 equal pieces. How long is each piece, in metres?
How many ten-thousands make one lakh?
A prize of ₹9,000 is shared equally among 6 winners. Each winner then donates ₹750 to charity. How much money does each winner keep?
questions.explanation: Each winner gets ₹9,000 ÷ 6 = ₹1,500. After donating, each keeps ₹1,500 − ₹750 = ₹750.

questions.q: Ishita multiplies 687 by 56. What answer should she get?

faq.q: What is the successor and predecessor of a number?
faq.a: The successor is one more and the predecessor is one less. Their difference is always 2.

faq.q: How do you round to the nearest 100?
faq.a: Look at the tens digit: 5 or more rounds up, otherwise round down. 462 → 500; 431 → 400.
